newsitem.title: UK: Tyco International to buy Inbrand for $320 million.
newsitem.headline: Tyco International to buy Inbrand for $320 million.

text.p: Diversified manufacturer Tyco International Ltd said Tuesday it agreed to acquire Inbrand Corp., a maker of disposable products for adult incontinence, in a stock transaction valued at $320 million.
The acquisition, to be accounted for as a pooling of interests, will be structured as a stock swap, with Inbrand shareholders receiving 0.43 share of Tyco stock for each Inbrand share.

Based on Tyco's May 12 closing price of $63.25, the terms of the agreement would result in a value of $27.20 per share, or a 70 percent gain, to Inbrand shareholders. The stock, which ended at $16 on Monday on Nasdaq, jumped $10 to $26 early on Tuesday.
Tyco's stock was unchanged at $63.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Inbrand manufactures adult incontinence products, as well as disposable diapers and feminine hygiene products.

Tyco said the acquisition would expand the presence of its Kendall Health Care Products unit, particularly in Europe, where it said Inbrand has a strong presence and fit with its strategy of expanding its four business segments through internal growth complimented by acquisitions.
"The many synergies between Kendall and Inbrand will result in an immediate positive impact on earnings," said Tyco Chairman and Chief Executive Dennis Kozlowski.
